analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend existing config/mcp-servers.json and core/conversation_models.py as base; add a token model module reusing design_tokens.py naming patterns; wire into intake API auth path (BI-0051) and MCP exposure (BI-0196) rather than new service stack.
dependency_findings: REQUIRES BI-0051 (auth on intake) as anchor for token validation
BLOCKS BI-0196 external MCP tool consumption (needs caller tokens)
RELATED BI-PF-0414 (store) for token persistence if needed
conflict_findings: BI-0051 touches intake/auth modules concurrently - coordinate token middleware insertion point
BI-PF-0412 worker store may share DB - avoid schema collisions
duplication_findings: BI-0051 already adds auth to intake API - align token validation there, don't duplicate
BI-0196 MCP exposure overlaps sharing surface - token model must gate MCP too
core/design_tokens.py is UI tokens, not auth tokens - no overlap, naming only
analysis.rationale: Foundational capability enabling MCP and intake sharing; extends existing config/model patterns instead of new infra.
assumptions: Existing intake auth (BI-0051) is the validation anchor
JWT-style bearer tokens suffice for v1
Config-driven token policy like other PF config/*.json
risks: Token scope model may be over-engineered for internal-only v1
Conflict with BI-0051 auth design if unspecified
evidence: config/mcp-servers.json exists as config-driven integration pattern
core/conversation_models.py shows model-layer pattern to extend
BI-0051 body covers auth+single-port for API consumers
missing_info: Token type: JWT vs opaque; issuer and rotation policy
External caller identity source (SSO, API keys, or per-org)
